chunks: From him, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'For the people of religion there are signs by which they are recognized: truthfulness in narration, fulfilling trusts, keeping promises, maintaining kinship ties, showing mercy to the weak, and sparing attention to women (or: sparing obedience to women), giving goodness, having good character, having broad character, following knowledge, and that which brings one close to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

Tooba is for them, and an excellent return. Tooba is a tree in Paradise; its root is in the house of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). There is no believer but that in his house is a branch from it. No desire for anything strikes his heart except that it comes to him with that. And if a diligent rider were to travel under its shade for a hundred years, he would not exit from it. And if a crow were to fly from its bottom, it would not reach its top until it falls down old.

So desire this! Indeed, the believer is preoccupied with himself, and people are at ease from him. When night covers him, he spreads his face and prostrates to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with the nobility of his body, whispering to the One who created him, for the freeing of his neck. So be like this.

key_terms.طُوبَى: Tooba (a tree in Paradise or a cry of happiness)

ai.seo_question: What are the recognized signs of a true believer according to Imam al-Sadiq (as)?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Imam al-Sadiq from Imam Ali, establishes the ethical markers of the 'people of religion' (ahl al-din), emphasizing truthfulness, trustworthiness, and familial ties as essential components of faith. It employs the metaphor of the Tooba tree to illustrate the spiritual stature of believers, whose roots are anchored in the Prophet's household, and highlights their devotion through night prayer (qiyam) as a means of self-reflection and divine intimacy. The text underscores the practical implication that true believers are occupied with their own spiritual growth, leaving others at ease, and encourages emulation of this state of constant worship and moral integrity.
